title: Updating quasi-Newton matrices with limited storage
contribution: Introduces the limited-storage ('special') BFGS update that keeps the last m (s, y) pairs, dropping the oldest at every iteration (the origin of L-BFGS, called SQN), proves positive definiteness, quadratic termination and a past-m secant property, and tests it in quasi-Newton and preconditioned-CG iterations (pp. 1-9).
problem_entry: Quasi-Newton storage n(n+1)/2 is too large; variable-storage CG methods need no structure but discard the quasi-Newton matrix and restart, so the entry is to remove that wholesale discard (p. 1).
key_idea: Write BFGS in product form H = v^T H v + rho s s^T so that dropping the oldest correction means v = I, rho s s^T = 0; keep the BFGS formula and line search unchanged (pp. 2-3).
assumptions: Smooth unconstrained f; y^T s > 0 each step (accurate enough line search, p. 2); quadratic termination and the secant property assume a strictly convex quadratic, conjugate steps and exact line searches (pp. 3-6); nonlinear local convergence only sketched for asymptotically exact searches (p. 7).
proof_devices: past-m secant equation H_k y_j = s_j from the identity v_i y_i = 0 (eqs. (6)-(7), pp. 3-4)
quadratic termination by showing SCG/SQN directions equal PCG with fixed preconditioner H0, induction from m+2 (eq. (14), pp. 5-6)
bounded condition number by transferring Fletcher's eigenvalue theorem (18): every special-update matrix is also a usual-BFGS matrix (pp. 6-7)
local convergence for nonlinear f asserted by analogy with Nazareth-Nocedal [9], not proved (p. 7)
experiments: Table I: function evaluations of CG, SCG (MSTORE 2/4/8), SQN (3/4/8), BFGS and Shanno on 6 Moré-type problems with n <= 20, same line search for all, competitors in the Shanno-Phua code; storage beyond BFGS run on purpose; SQN MSTORE=2 results withheld but declared (pp. 8-9).
positioning: Extends the Perry/Shanno/Buckley/Nazareth variable-storage line, criticising only their restart discard; credits Matthies-Strang for the H*g recursion and Fletcher/Stoer for the theory (pp. 1, 7, 9-10).
writing: Ten-page note; modest abstract ('some desirable properties'), unproved belief labelled as belief, conclusion slightly stronger than the 'few instances' caveat (pp. 1, 9).
limits_future: No global convergence proof; local convergence only sketched; tests only n <= 20; weak SQN m=2 results withheld; no future work stated (pp. 7-9).

title: Global convergence of a class of quasi-Newton methods on convex problems
contribution: Extends Powell's BFGS global convergence result to the restricted Broyden class with phi in [0,1) under Wolfe line searches (global, R-linear and Q-superlinear on uniformly convex f; lim inf for convex f), excluding DFP, and explains DFP's inferiority by the missing self-correcting term in the trace equation (pp. 1, 10-19).
problem_entry: Gap between theory and the methods as implemented: Powell's practical-line-search BFGS proof had not been extended to DFP or any other Broyden member; earlier results depend on the start matrix or on line searches no code uses (pp. 1-3).
key_idea: Track trace (large eigenvalues) and determinant (small eigenvalues) of B_k: a trace term shifts eigenvalues left in proportion to lambda_k/cos^2 theta_k for phi < 1 and is absent for DFP, giving self-correction (pp. 7-10).
assumptions: f twice continuously differentiable; uniformly convex on a convex level set (Assumption 2.1) for sections 3, 4, 6; convex, bounded below, bounded Hessian for section 5; Holder Hessian and unit step tried for superlinearity; Wolfe line search; any positive definite B1 (pp. 2-3, 14-15).
proof_devices: angle-based step and decrease bounds valid for any positive definite quasi-Newton update (Lemma 2.1, pp. 4-6)
steplength as ratio of model to true curvature (Lemma 2.2, p. 6)
trace equation (3.2) with term-by-term bounds, Goldfarb's ||y||^2/y^T s <= M (Lemma 3.1, pp. 7-8)
determinant identity (Pearson) plus AM-GM: steplengths bounded below in geometric mean (Lemma 3.2, pp. 9-10)
contradiction: cos theta -> 0 would drive the trace negative (Theorem 3.1, pp. 10-11)
R-linear rate by AM-GM on products of cos^2 (Lemma 4.2, pp. 12-13)
change of variables G(x*) = I by invariance, summability, Griewank-Toint Prop. 4 and Dennis-More characterization for superlinearity (pp. 11, 14)
excess term eta_k -> 0 reduces the convex case to the BFGS trace equation (Theorem 5.1, pp. 15-16)
experiments: One chosen 2-D uniformly convex function after Powell (1986), B1 = diag(1, 10^4); iterations to ||g|| <= 1e-4||g1|| rise from 15 toward thousands as phi -> 1 (OCR alignment lost); BFGS trace 10^4 -> 3 in 10 iterations vs DFP trace 1100 after 3000; small-eigenvalue control shows no difficulty (p. 18).
positioning: Generalizes Powell (1976); names the specific weakness of Dennis-More, Stoer, Ritter, Werner results; credits Xie Yuan-Fu's independent concurrent result; links to Powell's (1986) 2-D quadratic study (pp. 1-3, 17-18).
writing: Five-sentence abstract (assumption, result, exception, generalization, insight); insight claimed as a main contribution; intuition passages before theorems; DFP left as a plainly stated open problem (pp. 1, 3, 8-10, 19).
limits_future: Convexity needed and not known to be removable; rates not extended to the convex case; nonconvex result only local; DFP global convergence with practical line searches left open (pp. 3, 14, 19).

new_pattern_candidates.evidence: trace equation controls large eigenvalues, determinant controls small ones (S020); S002 bounds trace and determinant for L-BFGS

transferable: Write the trace of the updated matrix as a sum of signed terms and identify the term that shifts eigenvalues to the left; the member lacking it is the suspect (pp. 7-8, 17).

Assume G(x*) = I without loss of generality by affine invariance before a local-rate argument (p. 11).
Confirm a convergence-theory prediction with a one-function experiment that prints the quantity the proof tracks, plus the opposite case as a control (p. 18).
coauthors: Richard H. Byrd (Colorado), Ya-Xiang Yuan (Cambridge); thanks J. More and M. J. D. Powell (pp. 1, 19)

quotes.text: However there are some important gaps in what is understood about the behavior of these methods as implemented in practice.

Nevertheless, we have seen in this paper that the DFP method can be much less efficient than the BFGS method, and that the reason for this is that it lacks the self-correcting property given by the fourth term on the right-hand side of equation (3.2).

title: On the limited memory BFGS method for large scale optimization
contribution: Large-scale numerical study showing L-BFGS beats Buckley-LeNir and uses extra storage better, is greatly improved by simple dynamic scaling, competes with CG and (on CPU time) with partitioned quasi-Newton though PQN wins on evaluations when structure is supplied, plus an R-linear convergence proof on uniformly convex problems (pp. 2, 24-25).
problem_entry: Limited-memory methods had been compared only with CG; nothing was known about them against Newton or partitioned quasi-Newton on large problems, nor which limited-memory implementation is best (p. 3).
key_idea: Keep L-BFGS as close to BFGS as possible (unit step first, no forced interpolation, quadratic termination dropped) and add a cheap dynamic scaling of H0; then compare it head-to-head with the strongest neighbours (pp. 4-6, 13-15).
assumptions: Smooth f with analytic gradient, n large; convergence theorem needs f twice continuously differentiable, convex level set, uniform convexity bounds and bounded seed matrices B_k^(0) and inverses; low-accuracy stopping test (pp. 2, 7, 22-23).
proof_devices: every Hessian approximation is a bounded matrix updated at most m times by BFGS (p. 21)
uniform trace bound from ||y||^2/y^T s <= M2 over m updates (p. 23)
determinant lower bound via the Pearson/Powell formula (p. 23)
cos theta_k bounded below, then Powell-type decrease inequality gives R-linear rate for f and x (pp. 23-24)
theorem extended to backtracking line searches via Byrd-Nocedal and shown to cover Shanno-Phua and Buckley-LeNir as special cases (p. 24)
experiments: About 16 large test problems (Gill-Murray, More et al., Buckley-LeNir, Toint, Gilbert-Lemarechal, own matrix square root); competitors run at their authors' defaults; same-solution check; iterations/evaluations plus iteration/function/total time; win counts, speedup histograms, scaling rank tallies, very large runs on the Alliant FX/8; L-BFGS given a more accurate line search after diagnosing the rival's advantage; PQN with and without variable reduction; full data in companion report NAM 04; all digits lost in the text layer (pp. 6-20).
positioning: Places limited memory between CG and quasi-Newton; criticises Buckley-LeNir with a mechanism while conceding a newer Buckley code narrows the gap (Gilbert-Lemarechal); strongly praises Griewank-Toint PQN (pp. 3-4, 11, 24).
writing: Losses in the abstract; conclusions phrased as advice to users of the Harwell code; calibrated hedging; evidence explicitly bounded to the paper plus its companion report (pp. 2, 7, 15-18).
limits_future: R-linear is the best rate possible for L-BFGS; benefit of storage on very large problems unexplained; Gill-Murray scaling erratic and unreported; dynamic scaling named as perhaps the most important future topic (pp. 15-16, 24).

title: Global convergence properties of conjugate gradient methods for optimization
contribution: Proves global convergence (lim inf ||g|| = 0, nonconvex f, practical line searches, no restarts) for two families of nonlinear CG methods, |beta| <= beta_FR and nonnegative beta with Property (*) such as PR+, derives the PR-FR hybrid and a sufficient-descent line search, shows the conditions cannot be relaxed or combined, and confirms numerically that PR+ and PR-FR match PR while FR lags (pp. 4, 11-27).
problem_entry: A paradox: the inefficient FR method has a satisfactory convergence theory while the preferred PR/HS methods can cycle under steps any practical line search would accept (pp. 5-6).
key_idea: Keep the PR engine and change only beta and the line search's descent test: clip beta by beta_FR (PR-FR) or truncate it at zero (PR+), proving convergence for every method with the abstract Property (*) (pp. 11-12, 16, 20).
assumptions: Bounded level set; f continuously differentiable with Lipschitz gradient nearby; no convexity; Wolfe, strong Wolfe with sigma2 < 1/2, or ideal line search; section 4 assumes sufficient descent and iterates in the level set (pp. 6-9, 14).
proof_devices: Zoutendijk condition as hub and the template ||d_k||^2 grows at most linearly -> contradiction (Theorem 2.1 and section 2, pp. 7-8)
induction bound on <g,d>/||g||^2 with geometric sums of sigma2 (Lemma 3.1, p. 10)
sharpness via Powell's 1984 counterexample: |beta| <= c beta_FR with c > 1 fails (Proposition 3.3, pp. 12-13)
slowly changing directions: sum ||u_k - u_{k-1}||^2 < infinity (Lemma 4.1, pp. 15-16)
counting argument over windows of Delta steps: a fraction of steps not small (Lemma 4.2, pp. 17-18)
contradiction with bounded level set (Theorem 4.3, pp. 18-20)
intervals cannot be combined: modified Powell example and [-1,1] vs [0,inf) argument (pp. 20-21)
bump perturbation inside a ball avoided by the iterates gives a C-infinity strongly convex function with beta_PR < -beta_FR (Proposition 5.1, pp. 21-22)
experiments: Large test set (n >= 100, up to 10000); FR, PR-FR, PR, PR+ differing only in beta and line search; More-Thuente search with sigma2 = 0.1 chosen to satisfy Theorem 3.2, extended to enforce sufficient descent; same-solution filter; 'mod' column counting safeguard activations; PR+ best overall, FR clearly worst, restarts do not change the ranking; problem 45 shows FR's predicted tiny-step cycle (pp. 23-27; Tables 2-3 garbled).
positioning: Recasts Polak-Ribiere, Zoutendijk, Powell and Al-Baali as one approach; results built on Al-Baali and slightly stronger than Touati-Ahmed and Storey; PR+ credited to Powell (1985); Powell's restart criterion reinterpreted (pp. 6, 9, 11, 13, 20).
writing: Paradox stated in one sentence as motivation; scope exclusions up front; plain-words proof roadmap before lemmas; negative results beside positive ones (pp. 6, 12, 14, 20-22).
limits_future: Only lim inf, no rates; |beta| <= c beta_FR case open; families cannot be merged; 1969 strongly convex PR result not recovered (pp. 6, 12, 20-22).
